title: Genesis 23 — The death of Sarah and the purchase of the Makhpelah cave

verdicts.reasoning: Standard age-formula with additive *shanah* repetition (100+20+7) preserved correctly. ASV-baseline rendering, no philological issue.

The mourning-and-weeping doublet *li-spod l-Sarah v-li-vkotah* and the Qiryat-Arba/Hevron toponym-doubling are both preserved literally; the commentary documents the cross-corpus mourning-formula and the editorial-deliberateness of the toponym-doubling. Defensible scholarly rendering.
*Vayyaqom Avraham me-al p-nei meto* rendered as ASV-baseline; *bnei Chet* preserved as *sons of Het* per glossary policy.

The legal-status pair *ger v-toshav* (stranger and sojourner) is the standard ANE designation for resident-alien without inheritance-right; ASV rendering preserves the pair. Legal-formal idiom is correctly preserved.
Standard answer-formula; no philological issue.

citations: Targum Onqelos ad loc. (*rav min qodam YHWH*)
verdicts.reasoning: The construct *n-si Elohim* is HB hapax with four documented readings. The WoH literal *prince of Elohim* (reading a) is attested in Targum Onqelos, Vulgate, and Peshitta, against the modern critical superlative-default (Thomas 1953; Sarna; NJPS; NRSV). Choice is consistent with WoH standing policy on *Elohim*-bearing phrases and is defensibly grounded in the ancient versions. Multiple-reading apparatus held in glossary preserves the parallel.
*Vayyaqom Avraham vayyishtachu l-am ha-aretz li-vnei Chet* rendered ASV-baseline; *am ha-aretz* preserved via existing *eretz* glossary entry.
The idiom *im yesh et nafshekhem* (literally *if there is with your soul*) renders the volitional-*nephesh* sense as *if it be your desire* (ASV); defensible lexically.

The *me-arat ha-Makhpelah* toponym and the legal-symbolic *b-kesef male* formula both preserved with full apparatus; cross-corpus parallel at 1 Chr 21:24-25 documented. ANE-comparative legal-deed background (Westbrook, Tucker) correctly cited.

The gentilic-adjective *ha-Chitti* rendered as *the Hittite* preserving the lexical-form distinction from the collective-noun-phrase *bnei Chet*. The city-gate juridical-venue commentary aligns with Ruth 4:1-12 parallel. Defensible.
The triple performative *natatti lakh* (legal-fiction of gift) preserved as present-tense *I give*, against Avraham-s insistence on purchase. Captures the chapter-s narrative-legal tension correctly.
Standard bowing-formula; no issue.

The *natatti kesef ha-sadeh qach mimmenni* — Avraham-s counter-performative — rendered as ASV future *I will give the price*. Either present-performative or future is defensible; ASV convention preserved.
Routine answer-formula; no issue.

Efron-s rhetorical-deflection idiom *eretz arba me-ot shekel kesef beini u-veinkha mah hi* (a piece of land worth four hundred shekels of silver, what is that between me and you?) preserves the politeness-formula veneer over the actual price-statement. Defensible.

The *kesef over la-socher* pre-coinage bullion-formula correctly preserved as ASV *current money with the merchant*; cross-corpus parallel at 2 Kgs 12:5 documented; the verb *vayyishqol* (he weighed) lexically transparent in the pre-coinage system. The 400-shekel price commentary appropriately notes the editorial-undetermined character.

The conferment-formula *vayyaqom ... l-Avraham l-miqnah* with the ANE conveyance-document inventory-clause (field + cave + trees + borders) correctly identified as the legal-deed standing-clause. Tucker 1966 dialogue-deed classification is consensus scholarly position.
The witnessed-transfer clause *l-einei bnei Chet b-khol ba-ei sha-ar iro* with the city-gate juridical-venue and the Ruth 4:1-12 parallel correctly handled. Defensible.

First-interment-of-Sarah and the cross-corpus patriarchal-burial chain (Gen 25:9-10, 49:29-32, 50:13) correctly documented; the *hi Chevron b-eretz Kena-an* toponym-doubling closes the chapter-s geographical frame.
The recapitulating conferment-formula and the parashah-marker (setumah) closing correctly handled. Three-fold conferment-pattern at vv 17, 18, 20 noted as editorially-deliberate per Sarna.

citations: T. Bryce The Kingdom of the Hittites 2005

The literal *sons of Het* translation choice preserves the lexical-MT distinction and remains neutral on the historical-identification debate. Claim_type direct correctly assigned.

Eruvin 53a) are documentary; the Hebron-tomb identification via Josephus Antiquities I.237 + War IV.532 and the still-extant Herodian-period enclosure-walls is well-attested; the cross-corpus patriarchal-burial chain (Gen 25:9-10, 49:29-32, 50:13) verified. paragraphs.text: וַיִּהְיוּ֙ חַיֵּ֣י שָׂרָ֔ה מֵאָ֥ה שָׁנָ֛ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְשֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים שְׁנֵ֖י חַיֵּ֥י שָׂרָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the life of Sarah was a hundred years and twenty years and seven years; these were the years of the life of Sarah.

paragraphs.text: וַתָּ֣מָת שָׂרָ֗ה בְּקִרְיַ֥ת אַרְבַּ֛ע הִ֥וא חֶבְר֖וֹן בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וַיָּבֹא֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם לִסְפֹּ֥ד לְשָׂרָ֖ה וְלִבְכֹּתָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And Sarah died in Qiryat-Arba — the same is Hevron — in the land of Kena'an. And Avraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.

notes.official:
**The mourning-and-weeping doublet *li-spod l-Sarah v-li-vkotah*.** The verb-pair distinguishes *sapad* (formal lament, public eulogy — the *misped* of the funeral-ritual; cf. Gen 50:10 Egyptian-period mourning for Ya'aqov; 2 Sam 1:12 David's lament for Sha'ul and Yehonatan; 2 Sam 11:26 Bat-Sheva's *misped* for Uriah; Jer 16:5-6 the prophetic-prohibition of formal lament; Ezek 24:16-17 Ezekiel forbidden to mourn his wife) from *bakhah* (private weeping, affective grief). The ASV-baseline *to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her* preserves the two-verb distinction; the verbs are not interchangeable, and the pairing is a stylized HB mourning-formula rather than a redundancy. No glossary entry is required for the doublet itself; the formula is recognized across the HB.

**The *va-yavo Avraham* and the rabbinic *whence?* question.** The verb *va-yavo* (*and Avraham came*) implies that Avraham was elsewhere when Sarah died, and the question of *whence?* has generated a long exegetical tradition. Rashi at v 2, drawing on **Genesis Rabbah 58:5**, reads *va-yavo* against the Be'er-Sheva of Gen 22:19 (the last patriarchal-residence-notice before this chapter) — Avraham came from Be'er-Sheva to Hebron upon Sarah's death. The modern critical readings divide: **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 156 reads the *va-yavo* as the patriarchal arrival-at-the-mourning-site (a standard mourning-formula); **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 p. 372 reads the verb as narrative-scaffolding without locative implication. The question is reception-level; the translation preserves the literal *and Avraham came*.

**The Qiryat-Arba / Hevron toponym.** The double-naming (*b-Qiryat Arba hi Chevron*) is the chapter's first editorial-gloss identifying the older toponym *Qiryat Arba* (*city of Arba* — etiologically connected at Josh 14:15 to the giant Arba, *ha-adam ha-gadol ba-Anaqim*) with the canonical *Hevron*. The double-naming recurs at v 19 (the closing) and at Gen 35:27 (Ya'aqov's return to *Mamre Qiryat ha-Arba hi Chevron*). The toponym-doubling is editorially-deliberate.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֙קָם֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֣י מֵת֑וֹ וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל־בְּנֵי־חֵ֖ת לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And Avraham rose up from before his dead, and spoke to the sons of Het, saying,

paragraphs.text: גֵּר־וְתוֹשָׁ֥ב אָנֹכִ֖י עִמָּכֶ֑ם תְּנ֨וּ לִ֤י אֲחֻזַּת־קֶ֙בֶר֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם וְאֶקְבְּרָ֥ה מֵתִ֖י מִלְּפָנָֽי׃

i18n.en: I am a stranger and a sojourner with you; give me a possession of a burying-place with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲנ֧וּ בְנֵי־חֵ֛ת אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֥ר לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Het answered Avraham, saying to him,

paragraphs.text: שְׁמָעֵ֣נוּ ׀ אֲדֹנִ֗י נְשִׂ֨יא אֱלֹהִ֤ים אַתָּה֙ בְּתוֹכֵ֔נוּ בְּמִבְחַ֣ר קְבָרֵ֔ינוּ קְבֹ֖ר אֶת־מֵתֶ֑ךָ אִ֣ישׁ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ אֶת־קִבְר֛וֹ לֹֽא־יִכְלֶ֥ה מִמְּךָ֖ מִקְּבֹ֥ר מֵתֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of Elohim among us; in the choicest of our sepulchres bury your dead; none of us shall withhold from you his sepulchre, but that you may bury your dead.

notes.official:
***N'si Elohim atah b-tokhenu* — the Hittites' formal honorific to Avraham.** The construct phrase *n'si Elohim* admits four principal readings in the modern critical literature: (a) **literal-theological** — *a prince of Elohim*, one chosen or favored by the deity (Targum Onqelos *rav min qodam YHWH*, Vulgate *princeps Dei*, Peshitta *ris min Aloho*); (b) **superlative-Elohim** — *a mighty / exalted prince*, with *Elohim* as a Hebrew superlative-marker (the well-attested divine-name-superlative idiom — cf. *harerei El* Ps 36:7, *arzei El* Ps 80:11; **D. W. Thomas** *VT* 3 (1953) is the classical philological treatment); (c) **polytheist-context** — a Hittite-spoken designation in the speakers' own religious idiom; (d) **diplomatic-honorific** — a fixed-formula courtesy parallel to ANE diplomatic *your excellency*.

The modern critical default (Sarna, Westermann, NJPS, NRSV, ASV/KJV) is the superlative-reading (b): *a mighty prince*. The WoH translation preserves the literal *a prince of Elohim* (reading a), consistent with established WoH policy on *Elohim*-bearing phrases: where the MT preserves the lexeme *Elohim*, the WoH translation preserves it rather than collapsing to an English intensifier. The reading supports the patriarchal-narrative pattern of foreign-recognition of the patriarch's divine-standing (parallel to Avimelekh's *Elohim imkha b-khol asher atah oseh* at Gen 21:22).

The construct *n'si Elohim* is **HB hapax** — Gen 23:6 is its unique occurrence — which reinforces the editorial-distinctiveness of the honorific. See the glossary entry for the full cross-corpus distribution of *nasi* and the parallel divine-name-superlative constructions.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֧קָם אַבְרָהָ֛ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ לְעַם־הָאָ֖רֶץ לִבְנֵי־חֵֽת׃

i18n.en: And Avraham rose up, and bowed himself to the people of the land, to the sons of Het.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתָּ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־יֵ֣שׁ אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁכֶ֗ם לִקְבֹּ֤ר אֶת־מֵתִי֙ מִלְּפָנַ֔י שְׁמָע֕וּנִי וּפִגְעוּ־לִ֖י בְּעֶפְר֥וֹן בֶּן־צֹֽחַר׃

i18n.en: And he spoke with them, saying, If it be your desire that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and entreat for me to Ephron the son of Tsohar,

paragraphs.text: וְיִתֶּן־לִ֗י אֶת־מְעָרַ֤ת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה֙ אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּקְצֵ֣ה שָׂדֵ֑הוּ בְּכֶ֨סֶף מָלֵ֜א יִתְּנֶ֥נָּה לִ֛י בְּתוֹכְכֶ֖ם לַאֲחֻזַּת־קָֽבֶר׃

i18n.en: that he may give me the cave of Makhpelah, which he has, which is in the end of his field; for the full price let him give it to me in the midst of you for a possession of a burying-place.

notes.official:
**The cave-name *me'arat ha-Makhpelah*.** The toponym carries the definite article *ha-* attached to what appears to be a proper-name — a feature shared with a small set of HB toponyms (*ha-Negev*, *ha-Bashan*, *ha-Galil*) — suggesting either an originally-descriptive term crystallized into a place-name, or a place-name retaining the article. The etymological dispute: (a) the LXX-rabbinic *doubling* etymology, reading *Makhpelah* from *k-p-l* (*to double, fold*) and rendered LXX *to spēlaion to diploun* (*the double cave*); the rabbinic tradition develops the reading into the *double-chambered cave* (b. Eruvin 53a) or the cave large enough for the *doubled-couples* of patriarchal burials (Genesis Rabbah 58:8 — Avraham + Sarah, Yitzchaq + Rivkah, Ya'aqov + Le'ah, with Adam + Chavah as the foundational-couple in some traditions); (b) the modern critical default (Sarna, Westermann, Wenham, Hamilton) treats *ha-Makhpelah* as a proper-name with lost etymology. The Hebron-tomb identification (the present-day *Me'arat ha-Makhpelah* / *al-Haram al-Ibrahimi*) is supported by Josephus *Antiquities* I.237 and *War* IV.532 (the Herodian-period structure already standing in the 1st century CE), by the still-extant Herodian-period enclosure-walls, and by uninterrupted Jewish, Christian, and Muslim tradition. The cross-corpus patriarchal-burial chain — Avraham (Gen 25:9-10), Ya'aqov's burial-instructions naming the previously-interred (Gen 49:29-32), Ya'aqov's own burial (Gen 50:13) — grounds the multi-generational tradition.

***B-kesef male* — the full-price legal-symbolic formula.** Avraham's stipulation that he will purchase the cave *for the full price* is not mere politeness but legal-symbolic: by paying the full price (rather than accepting a gift, or paying a token), Avraham establishes an unambiguous and irrevocable transfer of title — one that cannot later be reclaimed by Efron's heirs or successors. The formula is the technical-legal seal of irrevocable transfer, with ANE-comparative parallels at Old Babylonian *kaspu gamru* (*full silver*) and Neo-Babylonian/Neo-Assyrian conveyance-formulae (Westbrook 1971 *JSS* 16, Tucker 1966 *JBL* 85, Petschow 1965 *MVAG*).

**The cross-corpus parallel at 1 Chr 21:24-25.** David, refusing Ornan's offer of the threshing-floor as a gift, insists on paying *b-kesef male* — verbally echoing Gen 23:9 — for the same legal-symbolic reason: cultically-significant land (in David's case, the future Temple-Mount) requires unambiguous title-transfer. **Sarna** 1989 p. 158 draws the Gen 23 / 1 Chr 21 parallel explicitly. **Jer 32:9-12** preserves the most-elaborated HB legal-conveyance pericope — Jeremiah's symbolic field-purchase at Anatot with weighed-silver and witnessed-deed.

paragraphs.text: וְעֶפְר֥וֹן יֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּת֣וֹךְ בְּנֵי־חֵ֑ת וַיַּעַן֩ עֶפְר֨וֹן הַחִתִּ֤י אֶת־אַבְרָהָם֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י בְנֵי־חֵ֔ת לְכֹ֛ל בָּאֵ֥י שַֽׁעַר־עִיר֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: Now Ephron was sitting in the midst of the sons of Het. And Ephron the Hittite answered Avraham in the ears of the sons of Het, of all that went in at the gate of his city, saying,

notes.official:
***Efron ha-Chitti* — the gentilic-adjective.** v 10 introduces Efron with the explicit gentilic *ha-Chitti* (*the Hittite*) — distinct from the collective-noun-phrase *bnei Het* used elsewhere in the chapter. The WoH translation renders *bnei Het* as *sons of Het* (literal) and *ha-Chitti* as *the Hittite* (the standard English convention for the gentilic), preserving the lexical-form distinction in the MT.

**The city-gate as juridical venue.** The phrase *l-khol ba'ei sha'ar iro* (*of all that went in at the gate of his city*) names the venue: the city-gate is the standard HB formal-juridical venue for property-transactions and legal-cases (cf. Ruth 4:1-12 — Boaz's redemption-at-the-gate, the most-elaborated HB city-gate-transaction-scene; Deut 21:19, 22:15, 25:7 — the elders-at-the-gate). The phrase locates the negotiation in the formal-public legal-arena and identifies the *bnei Het* as the witnessing-population — the necessary precondition for the conferment-formula at vv 17-18, 20.

paragraphs.text: לֹֽא־אֲדֹנִ֣י שְׁמָעֵ֔נִי הַשָּׂדֶה֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לָ֔ךְ וְהַמְּעָרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־בּ֖וֹ לְךָ֣ נְתַתִּ֑יהָ לְעֵינֵ֧י בְנֵי־עַמִּ֛י נְתַתִּ֥יהָ לָּ֖ךְ קְבֹ֥ר מֵתֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: No, my lord, hear me. The field I give you, and the cave that is in it, I give it to you; in the presence of the sons of my people I give it to you; bury your dead.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁתַּ֙חוּ֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם לִפְנֵ֖י עַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And Avraham bowed himself down before the people of the land.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר אֶל־עֶפְר֜וֹן בְּאָזְנֵ֤י עַם־הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַ֛ךְ אִם־אַתָּ֥ה ל֖וּ שְׁמָעֵ֑נִי נָתַ֜תִּי כֶּ֤סֶף הַשָּׂדֶה֙ קַ֣ח מִמֶּ֔נִּי וְאֶקְבְּרָ֥ה אֶת־מֵתִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה׃

i18n.en: And he spoke to Ephron in the ears of the people of the land, saying, But if you will, I pray you, hear me: I will give the price of the field; take it from me, and I will bury my dead there.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֧עַן עֶפְר֛וֹן אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֥ר לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Ephron answered Avraham, saying to him,

paragraphs.text: אֲדֹנִ֣י שְׁמָעֵ֔נִי אֶרֶץ֩ אַרְבַּ֨ע מֵאֹ֧ת שֶֽׁקֶל־כֶּ֛סֶף בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵֽינְךָ֖ מַה־הִ֑וא וְאֶת־מֵתְךָ֖ קְבֹֽר׃

i18n.en: My lord, hearken to me: a piece of land worth four hundred shekels of silver, what is that between me and you? Bury therefore your dead.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע אַבְרָהָם֮ אֶל־עֶפְרוֹן֒ וַיִּשְׁקֹ֤ל אַבְרָהָם֙ לְעֶפְרֹ֔ן אֶת־הַכֶּ֕סֶף אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר בְּאָזְנֵ֣י בְנֵי־חֵ֑ת אַרְבַּ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ שֶׁ֣קֶל כֶּ֔סֶף עֹבֵ֖ר לַסֹּחֵֽר׃

i18n.en: And Avraham hearkened to Ephron; and Avraham weighed out to Ephron the silver which he had named in the ears of the sons of Het, four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant.

notes.official:
***Kesef over la-socher* — the standardized-merchant-weight bullion-formula.** The phrase *over la-socher* (*passing for the merchant*) identifies the silver as conforming to the inter-regional commercial-standard weight, as distinct from local or domestic weights. Through the entire patriarchal-period and Iron-Age HB chronology — coinage was not introduced in the ANE until the late 7th / early 6th century BCE (Lydia) — silver functioned as bullion-money, valued and exchanged by weight. The chapter's verb *va-yishqol* (*and he weighed*) is grammatically and lexically transparent in the pre-coinage system: silver was *weighed out*, not *counted*. The *shekel* itself derives from *sh-q-l* (*to weigh*).

**The *over la-socher* formula is constrained in the HB** — it recurs only at 2 Kgs 12:5 (the Jehoash temple-repair fund — *kesef over*, the abbreviated form), confirming the formula's commercial-currency function. The wider HB pre-coinage land-transaction parallels: Gen 33:19 (Ya'aqov's *me'ah qesitah* purchase at Shechem; cf. *kesitah* glossary entry from Job 42); 2 Sam 24:24 / 1 Chr 21:25 (David's threshing-floor purchase, with the explicit *b-mishqal* — *by weight* — at 1 Chr); Jer 32:9-12 (Jeremiah's elaborate-procedure purchase at Anatot).

**The 400-shekel price.** The price is not trivial — comparable to the 50 shekels David pays for the threshing-floor (2 Sam 24:24), the 17 shekels Jeremiah pays at Anatot (Jer 32:9), or the 200-shekel range of standard Iron-Age field-prices attested in the Neo-Assyrian and Neo-Babylonian corpora. Whether the 400-shekel figure represents (a) a genuinely-elevated price reflecting the cultic significance of the burial-site, or (b) a stylized-large-number reflecting Avraham's stature, or (c) the price Efron extracts after rhetorical-deflection, is editorially-undetermined; Sarna 1989 p. 162 notes the price as *high* but does not commit. The chapter's emphasis is on the *full-payment* (the legal-symbolic transfer) rather than on the price-as-bargain.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣קָם ׀ שְׂדֵ֣ה עֶפְר֗וֹן אֲשֶׁר֙ בַּמַּכְפֵּלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י מַמְרֵ֑א הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וְהַמְּעָרָ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־בּ֔וֹ וְכָל־הָעֵץ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּכָל־גְּבֻל֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: So the field of Ephron, which was in Makhpelah, which was before Mamre — the field, and the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all the border of it round about, were made sure

notes.official:
**The conferment-formula *va-yaqem ... l-Avraham l-miqnah*.** vv 17-18 (continuing as a single legal-period across the verse-boundary) contain the chapter's formal legal-deed conferment-formula: the verb *va-yaqem* (qal of *q-w-m* with the inanimate-property subject — *and-it-stood / was-established / was-confirmed*) plus the *l-Avraham l-miqnah* construction (*to Avraham as a possession-by-purchase*) is the technical-juridical idiom of the conveyance-document genre. The chapter's careful enumeration here — *the field, and the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all the border of it round about* — is the standard ANE conveyance-document inventory-clause (the *object-of-sale* specification). The legal-formal weight is editorially-deliberate.

**The chapter as legal-narrative.** **G. M. Tucker** *JBL* 85 (1966) reads the entire chapter as a *dialogue-deed* — a literary-form derived from formal-conveyance documents, with the negotiation-dialogue replacing the document's witness-clause-and-stipulations and the conferment-formula at vv 17-18 (and the recapitulation at v 20) replacing the document's standing-clause. The classification has been broadly accepted (Westermann, Sarna, Wenham, Hamilton, Speiser). The ANE-comparative legal-deed parallels are well-documented (Old Babylonian sale-tablets, Neo-Babylonian/Neo-Assyrian conveyance-formulae, Aramaic Elephantine papyri, Hittite legal-deeds); the precise legal-tradition-of-origin is contested, with **Westbrook** 1971 *JSS* 16 arguing for the 1st-millennium Neo-Babylonian/Neo-Assyrian context as the closest formal-parallel and the older **Lehmann** 1953 *BASOR* 129 Hittite-law-parallel thesis substantially deflated by subsequent scholarship.

**The Hebron-Mamre identification.** The chapter locates the field *lifnei Mamre* (*before Mamre*) — the *elonei Mamre* (oaks/terebinths of Mamre) of Avraham's residence (Gen 13:18, 14:13, 18:1; see existing glossary entry). v 19 will make the identification explicit: *al-pnei Mamre hi Chevron*. The patriarchal-residence (the *elonei Mamre* of the three-visitors-theophany at Gen 18) and the patriarchal-burial-site are co-located at Hebron — the editorial-geography binds the Avraham-narrative's theophanic-peak (Gen 18) and its first formal land-acquisition (Gen 23) at a single site.

paragraphs.text: לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְמִקְנָ֖ה לְעֵינֵ֣י בְנֵי־חֵ֑ת בְּכֹ֖ל בָּאֵ֥י שַֽׁעַר־עִירֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: to Avraham for a possession, in the presence of the sons of Het, before all that went in at the gate of his city.

notes.official: **The witnessed-transfer clause *l-eynei bnei Het b-khol ba'ei sha'ar iro*.** The conferment-formula's closing element names the witnesses — *in the sight of the sons of Het, of all that went in at the gate of his city* — and locates the transaction at the formal-juridical venue (the city-gate, cf. v 10 commentary). The witnessed-transfer is the necessary precondition for the title's irrevocability: the *bnei Het* as witnessing-population establish the public-record of the conferment. The closest HB formal-parallel is **Ruth 4:1-12** — Boaz's redemption-and-marriage transaction at the city-gate of Bethlehem, with the witnessing-elders explicitly named (Ruth 4:9-11: *edim atem ha-yom* — *you are witnesses this day*) and the standing-clause pronounced. The Gen 23 and Ruth 4 parallels together constitute the HB's two most-elaborated formal-conveyance-narratives.

paragraphs.text: וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵן֩ קָבַ֨ר אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־שָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ אֶל־מְעָרַ֞ת שְׂדֵ֧ה הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֛ה עַל־פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵ֖א הִ֣וא חֶבְר֑וֹן בְּאֶ֖רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃

i18n.en: And after this, Avraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Makhpelah before Mamre — the same is Hevron — in the land of Kena'an.

notes.official:
**Sarah is the first interred in the Makhpelah cave** — the foundational burial that grounds the multi-generational patriarchal-burial-tradition. The cross-corpus chain that follows from this verse: Avraham himself is buried in the cave by Yitzchaq and Yishma'el (**Gen 25:9-10** — *va-yiqberu oto Yitzchaq v-Yishma'el banav el-me'arat ha-Makhpelah... ha-sadeh asher qanah Avraham me-et bnei Het*); Ya'aqov's burial-instructions on his deathbed name the previously-interred in the most extensive cross-reference (**Gen 49:29-32** — Ya'aqov names Avraham + Sarah, Yitzchaq + Rivkah, and his own first wife Le'ah as already-buried at the site, instructing his sons to bury him there *im-avotai*); Ya'aqov is buried in the cave by his sons after the Egyptian-period mourning (**Gen 50:13**). The pattern: the cave is the first piece of the promised-land actually purchased and held in title by the patriarchs (the editorial-significance of the chapter's careful legal-formalization) and the burial-site for three patriarchal couples — Avraham + Sarah, Yitzchaq + Rivkah, Ya'aqov + Le'ah.

The verse's closing formula *hi Chevron b-eretz Kena'an* repeats the v 2 toponym-doubling and adds the land-of-Kena'an locator — closing the chapter's geographical frame and binding the burial explicitly to the patriarchal-promise land (cf. the *eretz Kena'an* of the Avrahamic land-promise, Gen 12:5-7, 13:14-17, 15:7-21, 17:8). The first patriarchal-burial is in the promised-land itself — editorially significant for the multi-generational return-and-burial pattern (Ya'aqov's deathbed insistence on burial *im-avotai* at Hebron rather than in Egypt, Gen 47:29-31, 49:29-32, 50:5-14).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֨קָם הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה וְהַמְּעָרָ֧ה אֲשֶׁר־בּ֛וֹ לְאַבְרָהָ֖ם לַאֲחֻזַּת־קָ֑בֶר מֵאֵ֖ת בְּנֵי־חֵֽת׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the field, and the cave that is in it, were made sure to Avraham for a possession of a burying-place by the sons of Het.

notes.official:
**The chapter's recapitulating conferment-formula.** v 20 repeats the *va-yaqem ... l-Avraham la-achuzat qaver me-et bnei Het* in a compact summary-form. The three-fold conferment-pattern across vv 17, 18, and 20 is editorially-deliberate: the chapter's legal-formalization is so important to the patriarchal-narratives' theological structure — the first piece of the promised-land actually held in title — that the conferment is restated for emphasis (Sarna 1989 pp. 162-163). The closing *me-et bnei Het* (*from the sons of Het*) names the conveying-party explicitly, sealing the title-transfer's documentary completeness.

**The chapter's closing parashah-marker (ס).** The petuhah/setumah closing-marker (ס for *setumah*, *closed*) marks the chapter as a self-contained narrative-unit in the Masoretic parashah-division. The next narrative-unit (Gen 24 — the betrothal-mission for Yitzchaq) presupposes Sarah's burial and the establishment of the patriarchal-tomb at Hebron, but is a distinct narrative-act.
